subject: Dedicated capacity conflict resolution: Aurum / BrightCloud
messages:
From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@aurum.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity request — Aurum & BrightCloud overlapping windows

Hi Rafael / Monica,

Quick context: we have a firm launch window for DL-4982 (Aurum) late July. Our GTM requires a dedicated GPU pool for steady-state inference at 1.2k concurrent sessions during peak. We just learned BrightCloud (DL-5021) also expects a dedicated pool with overlapping peak hours.

Attached is our formal request (aurum_capacity_request.xlsx) with the preferred start date (2027-07-15) and run-rate commit. We understand capacity is constrained — looking for a path to secure the minimum guaranteed capacity or a time-slice alternative. Key asks:
- Confirm whether you can reserve N4 instances (8xA100 equivalent) for Aurora pool July–Q3.
- If not, propose an alternative (time-slice, burst credit, or smaller instance + quantized model).
- SLA/latency guarantee for 99th pct tail under dedicated allocation.

We’re on a tight cadence; can someone confirm by EOD Friday (7/2)? Happy to jump on a short call.

Thanks,
Elena Garcia
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurum AI
Attachment: aurum_capacity_request.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@aurum.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — Aurum & BrightCloud overlapping windows

Team — looping you in to triage. Summary: Aurum (DL-4982) submitted a formal dedicated request for mid-July start. BrightCloud already has a pending commit (DL-5021) with overlapping peak hours. We have finite Dedicated pools in the US-West cluster next month; raw GPU headroom is limited.

Options I see (quick):
1) Pro-rata split by committed GPU-hours (short-term) — minimizes churn but reduces peak for both.
2) Time-sliced dedicated windows (day/night split) — preserves peak for each during allocated hours.
3) Prioritize by contract (commit size / ARR / escalation) and move one customer to best-effort + burst credits.
4) Offer a lower-cost quantized model variant for one customer to reduce static GPU footprint + performance guardrails.

I attached a proposed_allocations.csv with a rough split and suggested burst windows. Marcus / Vivek — what do you need from procurement/legal to adjust SLA or give temporary exceptions? Karthik — if we time-slice, what changes to infra routing and cache warming are required (cost/latency tradeoffs)?

We need a decision this week to communicate to both customers and avoid launch delays. Propose a 30-minute triage at 11:00 PST if that works for everyone.

- Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_allocations.csv (csv)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — Aurum & BrightCloud overlapping windows

On Tue, Jun 30, 2027 at 10:01 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — looping you in to triage. Summary: Aurum (DL-4982) submitted a formal dedicated request for mid-July start. BrightCloud already has a pending commit (DL-5021) with overlapping peak hours. We have finite Dedicated pools in the US-West cluster next month; raw GPU headroom is limited.

Thanks for the summary. A couple of data points:
- Per our ARR and signed commit, Aurum’s $/GPU-hour value is ~25% lower than BrightCloud, but BrightCloud’s overall ARR with us is larger.
- If we evaluate by incremental ARR per GPU-hour, BrightCloud yields higher short-term revenue density.

Recommendation (practical):
- Short-term (July launch): do a time-slice. Aurum gets weekday business hours (0800–2000 PST) for the first 30 days. BrightCloud gets nights/weekends + negotiated daytime patching windows. This avoids breaking both launches.
- Simultaneously, offer Aurum a 20% discount on additional burst capacity for the first 60 days and a commitment path to full Dedicated in Q4.
- If either party pushes for exclusive Dedicated before Q4, escalate to Sales leadership for one-time exception + financial compensation from the other party.

I attach arr_per_gpu_calcs.pdf with the revenue density math. Also pushing the quantized model path — can reduce GPU footprint by ~35% at modest latency increase (documented).

Marcus
Director, Deals & Capacity Strategy
Attachment: arr_per_gpu_calcs.pdf (pdf)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@aurum.ai>, Sasha Petrov <sasha@brightcloud.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity request — Aurum & BrightCloud overlapping windows

Begin forwarded message:

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP / time-slice proposal

Hi Elena / Sasha —

Thanks for the flag and for being flexible. To avoid blocking both launches, Redwood proposes the following mutual action plan (MAP) to share the US-West Dedicated pool while we scale additional capacity:

Option B (preferred by Redwood ops): Time-sliced Dedicated windows
- Aurum (DL-4982): Weekdays 08:00–20:00 PST (primary serving window).
- BrightCloud (DL-5021): Weeknights 20:00–08:00 PST + full access weekends.
- 24/7 burst pool of 4xA100-equivalent for emergency failover (finite and metered).
- Traffic shaping rules + KV prefix segregation to avoid cache thrash.
- SLA amendments: 99th tail latency during allocated window — guaranteed; outside window best-effort with defined burst credits.

Next steps: please review the attached MAP_doc.pdf and approve or send counter-proposal by 7/2 EOD. We will prepare a short amendment for signature and schedule a technical cutover call 7/6–7/8.

If either party requires exclusive Dedicated immediately, we will escalate to Sales leadership for a short-term carve (with offsetting financial terms).

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP_doc.pdf (pdf)

End forwarded message.
From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@aurum.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — Aurum & BrightCloud overlapping windows

Monica / Rafael —

Thanks for the quick work and the MAP. Aurum is broadly OK with the time-slice Option B for the initial 30-day launch window provided we get the following in writing:
1) 99th tail latency SLA during our allocated window (weekday 08:00–20:00 PST).
2) 6 hours of guaranteed burst credits (use-anytime) in the first 30 days.
3) A clear escalation path with named contacts if we see degraded tail latencies.

If you can get those in an amendment (even a 1-pager), we will accept and sign quickly — otherwise we risk delaying launch. Also would like a confirmation that cache warming will be performed ahead of our peak window each day.

Please send the amendment link and the cutover-call invite.

Best,
Elena Garcia
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurum AI
